world: Use case: stylized-concept. Production pixel art tileset for Ashen Veil, side-view samurai platformer. ONE 1536x1024 sprite atlas divided into a precise 3 column x 2 row grid of equally sized 512x512 cells. Solid pure magenta #FF00FF background. Each cell contains ONE isolated object, fully inside cell with generous padding. Top row: wide dark blue stone platform cap with red moss and deep brick foundation; wide Japanese timber balcony ledge supported by beams; wide craggy basalt ledge with glowing ember fissures. Bottom row: distant Japanese castle silhouette cluster; dark bamboo grove silhouette cluster; jagged mountain peak silhouette cluster. Strict authentic 16-bit pixel art drawn on coarse 128x128 grid per cell then nearest-neighbor enlarged 4x. Extremely crisp visible square pixels. 16 shared colors: navy-black, slate blue, muted crimson, burnt orange, ivory. Hard cel shading, NO gradients, NO painted texture, NO brush strokes, NO soft lighting, NO anti-aliasing. No actors, no text, no UI. Side view, orthographic. Platform walkable tops perfectly horizontal. Complete assets with nothing clipped.
ui: Use case: stylized-concept. Production UI atlas for Ashen Veil samurai pixel-art game. ONE 1536x1024 image divided exact 3 columns by 2 rows, each cell 512x512. Solid pure magenta #FF00FF outside objects. Top row cells: wide rectangular dark navy stone menu button with thin ivory pixel bevel and tiny crimson corner accents; same wide button selected with ember orange interior; large square dark navy inset panel with simple stepped pixel corner frame. Bottom row cells: compact ivory four-direction cross icon with dark outline; compact square crimson sword button with ivory katana icon; compact square slate-blue jump button with ivory up arrow. Center each object with large magenta padding. Authentic 16-bit low-resolution pixel art designed on a 128x128 grid per cell, nearest-neighbor upscaled 4x. Visible chunky square pixels, straight crisp boundaries, hard flat 3-step shading. Restrained navy slate crimson ivory palette. NO text, no letters, no rounded vector shapes, no gradients, no brush strokes, no painterly shading, no soft lighting. Reusable game interface sprite assets.
campaignMap: Production asset: a top-down OVERWORLD CAMPAIGN MAP for the MAIN MENU of a samurai game called Ashen Veil. NOT a side-scroller scene. Authentic very crisp 16-bit pixel art, visibly chunky square pixels, 24-color palette navy, slate blue, muted crimson foliage, warm ivory, moss green. 1536x1024 landscape canvas. Ten distinct geographical regions arranged in EXACT five columns by two rows. Each region occupies its own 307x512 rectangular area but NO UI panel borders; together they form one coherent archipelago world map on dark navy water. Top row from left: monastery island, bamboo wetlands, fortified stone ramparts, volcanic aqueduct, flooded cistern ruins. Bottom row: storm temple, crimson garden, obsidian keep, snowy mountain ascent, final bell citadel. Each region has small detailed top-down pixel buildings/trees/cliffs near its upper edge, with a very clear open winding dirt path through the middle and lower area for ten level buttons to be overlaid later by game engine. Paths and small rope bridges connect regions. Keep buildings small; this is an explorable world MAP, no close-up scenes. No numbers, no labels, no letters, no buttons, no actors, no HUD. NO painted textures, NO brushed gradients, NO antialiasing, NO photographic details, NO smooth illustration. All terrain made of crisp square pixel clusters, game tileset aesthetic.
